issues.title: Undefined initial-value trial space

failure_location.quote: the initial value $U_0\in X_{h,X}$ is the solution

issues.failure_explanation: The initialization contract places U_0 in X_{h,X}, a space never defined in the old source. The surrounding construction defines only X_{h,H}, and both the time-stepping unknowns and the tests in the initialization equation belong to X_{h,H}. Thus the algorithm does not literally specify a trial space for U_0.
issues.overall_effect: The fully discrete scheme is ill-typed at k=0, so the stability lemma, the initial-value estimates, and the global and local error results cannot literally be instantiated for the stated algorithm.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In the initialization sentence, replace X_{h,X} by the already defined X_{h,H}, so U₀ lies in the same finite-element space used for the time-stepping unknowns and test functions. No proof or estimate needs alteration.
issues.why_classification: The old source uniquely forces X_{h,H}: it is the only defined discrete space, and both Uₖ and the tests in the initialization equation belong to it. The wrong subscript is transcriptional, and the entire listed dependent chain applies unchanged after correction.

issues.title: Missing domain geometry in the elliptic-regularity sufficient condition
issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that A in C^{0,1}(D) alone guarantees Assumption I throughout the old bounded-domain setting. The old paper actually assumes the global H^2 estimate in Assumption I and gives no valid derivation of it from coefficient regularity alone. For a bounded planar sector of opening 3π/2, take A=I and a cutoff of r^{2/3} sin(2θ/3) that vanishes near the outer arc. This function lies in H_0^1 but not H^2, while its negative Laplacian is in L^2 because the cutoff error is supported away from the reentrant corner. Hence the corresponding Dirichlet solution violates Assumption I despite A being constant and Lipschitz. The missing material condition is boundary geometry or equivalent elliptic regularity.
issues.overall_effect: The remark gives false applicability guidance, although the later formal theorems remain conditional on Assumption I and therefore are not themselves defeated by this prose error.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Qualify the applicability remark locally: in addition to A being Lipschitz, require boundary geometry that provides global Dirichlet H² regularity for A and Aᵀ, with a C^{1,1} domain as a standard sufficient example. Keep all later results conditional on Assumption I.
issues.why_classification: Coefficient regularity alone fails on natural, substantial bounded-domain classes such as domains with reentrant corners, so adding geometry meaningfully narrows the stated applicability and is not a minor technical qualification. The corrected sufficient condition remains recognizably comparable, and the repair is contained because all formal results already assume Assumption I; thus neither global reconstruction nor major mathematical loss is required.

issues.title: Ill-typed subdomain quantifier in the local measure lemma
issues.failure_explanation: The lemma quantifies K as an element of D even though it immediately forms L^2(K), η(K), and the measure |K|. An element of D is a point, not the measurable subdomain required by those expressions, so the literal statement has an invalid input type.
issues.overall_effect: The local measure lemma is malformed, and its stated form cannot support the localization estimates in Lemma 3.2 or the resulting global error theorem.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the quantifier by “for any measurable subset K ⊂ D.” The lemma and every listed use of it can otherwise remain unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The expressions L²(K), η(K), and |K| uniquely force K to be a set rather than a point of D. Replacing the membership relation by set inclusion repairs only the transcription and requires no change to the lemma's reasoning or its dependent estimates.

issues.title: Undefined exponent in the Meyers-regularity lemma
issues.failure_explanation: The formal result quantifies an exponent p>2 and uses p in the data spaces and the ensuing norm estimate. The exponent r in the membership conclusion is never introduced or related to p, so the literal conclusion is undefined and does not state the W^{1,p} regularity advertised by the estimate.
issues.overall_effect: The cited regularity lemma is malformed and does not literally provide the p-regularity used in the surrounding applicability discussion. The subsequent local theorem explicitly assumes W^{1,p} regularity, so its conditional statement is not a dependent failure.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace W_0^{1,r}(D) by W_0^{1,p}(D) in the membership conclusion, using the exponent p already quantified by the lemma.
issues.why_classification: The old statement introduces only p, uses p in the data spaces, and immediately gives a W^{1,p} estimate. These surrounding formulas uniquely force r to be p, so no mathematical inference or regularity argument must be repaired.

issues.title: Undefined selector in the no-scale-separation coefficient

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The time-independent rough diffusion coefficient $a^\varepsilon(x)$ lies in $\mathcal{M}(\lambda, \Lambda; D)$

issues.failure_explanation: The numerical construction requires a bounded selector that equals one on K_0 and zero outside. The old source never defines δ_{K_0}; if read as a Dirac-type object, it is a distribution rather than an L^∞ coefficient and makes 1-δ_{K_0} unsuitable for this piecewise diffusion formula. The characteristic function χ_{K_0} supplies the required bounded selector.
issues.overall_effect: The coefficient for the final old-version experiment is not literally a valid bounded diffusion coefficient, so that experiment is not executable or reproducible from the stated formula. The analytical results are unaffected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace both occurrences of δ_{K_0} in the coefficient formula by χ_{K_0} and identify χ_{K_0} as the characteristic function of K₀. No other part of the experiment or analysis needs modification.
issues.why_classification: The bounded-diffusion contract and the piecewise defect construction uniquely require an indicator-type selector, and the old source already uses χ for characteristic cutoffs. Correcting the symbol yields the forced bounded coefficient without a new construction, inference, or change of guarantee.

issues.title: Conflicting numerical time-step declarations

failure_location.quote: To study the macroscopic error, we set $h=1/1000$ and $\Delta t=0.2$.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We fix the time step $\Delta t =0.02$, and vary $h$ and $H$.

issues.failure_explanation: The local Example 1 prose claims that the macroscopic computation used Δt=0.2. The governing numerical setup says all examples fix Δt=0.02, and the same example's microscopic setup also uses 0.02. These declarations cannot all describe one section-wide parameter convention, so the old paper does not establish an unambiguous time step for reproducing the experiments. The new version resolves the mismatch in favor of 0.02.
issues.overall_effect: The reported spatial-convergence experiments cannot be reproduced or interpreted unambiguously with respect to temporal discretization, although no analytical theorem is affected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Check the computational record for the affected Example 1 run and make all of its time-step declarations agree with the value actually used. On the contained route supported by the section-wide setup, change the local Δt=0.2 declaration to Δt=0.02 and confirm that the reported table was generated with Δt=0.02.
issues.why_classification: The incompatible declarations do not uniquely determine the actual run parameter from the old source, so this is not a transcriptionally forced typo. Resolving it requires a genuine but routine local check and consistent reporting; it affects no analytical result and preserves the experiment and its convergence interpretation once the actual time step is recorded.
